# Add immutable per-group transaction history and cursor

## Context

D#18224 measured `data.Store` versus `collection.Base` at depth 50 over the real Workstation document: latency differed only 1.04x, while mutability was decisive. Store insertion writes an internal id and Models expose replacement setters; frozen plain rows in a Collection can be the append-only authority.

## The Problem

There is no user-facing dock history. Adding a mutable Store as authority would permit whole-field replacement of retained transactions, while statically importing it would make single-window/history-disabled apps pay for unused machinery. Cursor, redo invalidation, eviction, and retirement are Group-local invariants, not global filters.

## The Architectural Reality

A Group owns one bounded history and cursor. The authoritative vehicle is a `collection.Base` of recursively frozen plain records. A `data.Store` may be created lazily as a read-only projection for grids/Neural Link inspection, but it never drives adoption or cursor decisions. A Group-level Provider publishes derived command state.

## The Fix

Implement generic History/Group cursor semantics: append, undo, redo, redo-tail invalidation, depth eviction, immutable serialization, and provider projections. Dynamically load the history module at the first admitted transaction; the load is an admission barrier and queues the original descriptor exactly once. `historyDepth: 0` imports nothing.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| authoritative history | D#18224 H2 | frozen plain rows in `collection.Base` | disabled at depth 0 | JSDoc | nested + whole-field mutation controls |
| cursor | D#18224 criteria 7/8 | Group-local undo/redo/append/preserve | bounds fail closed | JSDoc | branch/eviction unit matrix |
| Provider state | explicit cross-window Provider parent | `canUndo`, `canRedo`, depth/status | false/empty before load | guide/JSDoc | multi-window binding arm |
| optional Store view | manager.Store precedent | lazy read-only clones | destroy/rebuild loses no truth | JSDoc | mutation cannot affect authority |
| module admission | D#18224 criterion 13 | await once before mutation; enqueue once | load failure leaves no mutation | JSDoc | red control at first gesture |

## Decision Record impact

Depends on amended ADR 0029; no new ADR.

## Decision Record

Required prerequisite: the #18303 hard-cut authority leaf.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

Owns criteria 1–3's H2 vehicle, single-window cost, bounded history, and cursor half of criterion 7.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] History rows are recursively frozen after Collection admission and reject nested mutation and whole-field replacement.
- [ ] Append after undo drops only the redo tail; depth eviction and cursor bounds are Group-local and deterministic.
- [ ] Frozen bytes emitted for a retained row remain unchanged after every rejected mutation control.
- [ ] `historyDepth: 0` causes zero static/dynamic history-module loads and leaves single-window behavior byte-equivalent.
- [ ] The first enabled transaction awaits one dynamic import before participant mutation and enqueues its original descriptor exactly once.
- [ ] The Group Provider exposes correct `canUndo` / `canRedo` in every bound window without presentation sweeps.
- [ ] Any TransactionStore is lazy, read-only, clone-fed, and disposable without changing authority.

## Out of Scope

Participant adoption, native effects, persisted topology snapshots, or Neural Link command migration.

## Avoided Traps

No mutable Model authority; no global Store filtered by Group; no eager import; no second cursor in a UI projection.

Part of #18303. Blocked by the hard-cut and Group-binding leaves.

- 2026-09-05T12:09:36Z @neo-fable-mnemosyne referenced in commit `f27b2ef` - "feat(manager): history depth is the Group's own choice, a cursor moves only after its row was applied, and the History owns its rows (#18310)

Three boundaries from the epic owner and the Group's author, folded before
this branch becomes a PR.

Depth is Group-local: `setHistoryDepth({groupId, depth})` sets one Group's
bound before its first write and is refused once its history loaded; the
worker-wide `historyDepth` stays the default a Group is born with, so two
independent roots of one app in one worker never take each other's policy
through admission order.

undo/redo take `apply(row)` and run it inside the queued step: the row a move
would return is read first, the application runs, and only when it resolved
does the cursor move and the provider publish — a rejected application leaves
both where they were, and a move without an application is refused. `write`
keeps its shape and states that its body is provisional: the participant
protocol lands there as one step under one owner, compensation across a
failed append included; nothing outside may depend on its parts being
separate.

History extends core.Base and owns a private Collection instead of extending
one, so the only writes that reach a row are append, undo and redo — the
inherited remove/insert/splice/sort surface no longer exists on the
authority. `rows` hands out a fresh array; `peek(direction)` shows a move's
row without moving. The class hierarchy is regenerated for the new parent."

- 2026-09-05T15:07:35Z @neo-fable-mnemosyne referenced in commit `7a11ffc` - "fix(manager): a refused row leaves the history untouched, the bound is a finite positive integer, and a pending history import is fenced by Group retirement (#18310)

Round 1 of the review on the Group history leaf. Three executed controls fell: a descriptor that reads as plain data but cannot be structured-cloned (a Proxy) was refused only after the redo tail was dropped and the sequence advanced; Infinity, NaN and fractional bounds reached the log through a direct History or the manager's worker-wide default; a Group retired while its history module was still loading received a History on completion, registered with no owner to release it.

History#append now runs every fallible step first — assertRow, then the structured copy of the stamped descriptor — and only then drops the redo tail, adds the row, advances the sequence and moves the cursor, so a refusal leaves rows, bytes, cursor, sequence and redo tail exactly as they were. The bound is validated as a finite positive integer at construction (a throw, before the instance exists) and on assignment with the house idiom for a refused config value — logged, the bound in force stays — because a throwing beforeSet leaves the refused value staged in the config store; the manager's historyDepth default takes the same shape with zero as the disabled mode. loadHistory checks the Group is still registered when the import settles and creates nothing for a retired one; the write that waited rejects at its liveness check.

Controls: the Proxy refusal with byte-identical log; construction and assignment refusals for every invalid bound on both surfaces plus exact eviction at depth 2; the import held pending, the Group retired, the import resolved — write rejected, nothing adopted, the instance registry unchanged, and the live control creating and releasing exactly one History."
